bib.title: ViLBERT: Pretraining Task-Agnostic Visiolinguistic Representations for Vision-and-Language Tasks

legacy_report:
SOURCE: ViLBERT: Pretraining Task-Agnostic Visiolinguistic Representations for Vision-and-Language Tasks. Jiasen Lu, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Stefan Lee. This file is **arXiv:1908.02265v1 (6 Aug 2019), marked "Preprint. Under review."** It is not the NeurIPS 2019 camera-ready, and numbers may differ from the published version.

COVERAGE: Read all 45,954 of 45,954 chars, all 11 pages. There is no appendix. I skimmed the references only for where the method comes from.

CLAIMS
- claim: The design is two streams, one per modality, joined by co-attention layers that swap keys and values between them. Text gets more processing before fusion, because region features are already high-level.
  number: none
  setup: Text stream is BERT-base. Visual stream has hidden size 1024 and 8 heads. Interaction happens only at Co-TRM layers.
  quote: "the keys and values from each modality are passed as input to the other modality's multi-headed attention block"; "the text stream has signiﬁcantly more processing before interacting with visual features" (p.4)
  where: p.4, Fig. 2b
- claim: The image goes in as 10 to 36 detector region features: Faster R-CNN with a ResNet-101 backbone, pretrained on Visual Genome. Each region also gets a 5-d spatial vector, and an IMG token stands for the whole image.
  number: 10–36 regions
  setup: Regions kept above a confidence threshold. Each feature is the mean-pooled conv feature of its region. The 5-d vector (normalised box corners plus fraction of image area) is projected and summed with it.
  quote: "We use Faster R-CNN [31] (with ResNet-101 [11] backbone) pretrained on the Visual Genome dataset [16] ... keep between 10 to 36 high-scoring boxes." (p.5); "constructing a 5-d vector from region position (normalized top-left and bottom-right coordinates) and the fraction of image area covered" (p.4)
  where: p.4–5
- claim: Pretraining uses about 3.1M Conceptual Captions pairs (3.3M nominal, minus broken links) and two tasks. The first masks words and regions, and a masked region is trained to match the detector's class distribution (KL loss) rather than to rebuild its features. The second predicts whether an image and caption are aligned, with negatives made by swapping one side.
  number: ~15% masking; 3.1M pairs
  setup: 8 TitanX GPUs, batch size 512, 10 epochs, Adam at 1e-4, the two losses weighted equally.
  quote: "masking approximately 15% of both words and image region inputs"; "our model is trained with around 3.1 million image-caption pairs" (p.4–5)
  where: p.4–5
- claim: Fine-tuning with a single added head beats the task-specific SOTA on all four tasks.
  number: VQA 70.55 test-dev vs DFAF 70.22. VCR Q→AR 54.04 vs R2C 43.1. RefCOCO+ val 72.34 vs MAttNet 65.33. Flickr30k R1 58.20 vs SCAN 48.60.
  setup: Table 1. For VQA and VCR the comparison uses ViLBERT's val/test-dev figures. RefCOCO+ reranks Mask R-CNN proposals. Retrieval is trained 4-way multiple choice on Flickr30k.
  quote: "We set state-of-the-art for VCR, RefCOCO+ and image retrieval by signiﬁcant margins (7-10 percentage points improvement)" (p.7)
  where: p.7, Table 1
- claim: Two streams beat one shared BERT stack, both with and without pretraining. Pretraining itself adds 2–13%.
  number: VQA 68.85 for single-stream vs 70.55 for ViLBERT. VQA 68.93 for ViLBERT without pretraining (ViLBERT†).
  setup: The single-stream baseline is initialised from BERT-base and trained identically. It was not tested on retrieval because of compute cost.
  quote: "Our models further improve by between 2% and 13% across tasks when using a ViLBERT model that has been pretrained" (p.7)
  where: p.7
- claim: Results improve steadily with pretraining data, and zero-shot retrieval beats the fine-tuned prior SOTA on R1. The best number of Co-TRM→TRM blocks depends on the task.
  number: Zero-shot R1 is 0.00 at 0%, 20.40 at 25%, 26.76 at 50% and 31.86 at 100% of the data. VQA goes from 68.93 to 70.55 over the same range.
  setup: Random 25% and 50% subsets of Conceptual Captions (Table 3). Zero-shot means no Flickr30k fine-tuning. On depth, VQA and retrieval peak around 6 blocks, while VCR and RefCOCO+ prefer shallower models (Table 2).
  quote: "accuracy grows monotonically as the amount of data increases"; "31.86 vs 48.60 R1 for prior SOTA" (p.7–8)
  where: p.7–8, Tables 2–3

LIMITS
- Each configuration is a single run. There are no variance figures or significance tests.
- Test-server results (VQA, VCR) are reported only for the full model.
- The detector and its region features stay frozen; the image is never processed end to end. The paper does not ablate how many regions are kept or which detector is used.
- The paper concedes several gaps:
  - It uses BERT-base, not large, because of training time.
  - It does not cover generation, dialog, embodied or video tasks.
  - "it is unclear how to effectively decode output text from our bidirectional model".
  - Conceptual Captions captions are noisy and editorialised.
- The data-scaling evidence covers only 25%, 50% and 100%, so it says nothing beyond 3.1M pairs.
- Dated: the fusion-encoder approach of frozen detector regions plus cross-attention was later replaced by grid/ViT patch features, contrastive encoders (CLIP) and decoder LLMs (LLaVA). Nothing here is compared with those.

BUILDS ON
- BERT (Devlin et al., arXiv 2018)
- Transformer (Vaswani et al., NeurIPS 2017)
- Bottom-up/top-down region features (Anderson et al., CVPR 2018)
- Faster R-CNN (Ren et al., NeurIPS 2015)
- Visual Genome (Krishna et al., arXiv 2016)
- Conceptual Captions (Sharma et al., ACL 2018)
- VideoBERT (Sun et al., arXiv 2019), named as concurrent work in the single-stream style

CODE: none in the paper.

FIGURES: Fig. 2, "We introduce a novel co-attention mechanism based on the transformer architecture. By exchanging key-value pairs in multi-headed attention..." (p.3). A standard encoder block drawn next to the co-attention block shows the Q/K/V swap at a glance. Fig. 1 (p.2, the two-stream overview with regions and an IMG token) is a backup choice. I took both captions from the text extraction and did not run figures.py.

PROBLEMS
- Citation numbers are wrong in places:
  - Co-attention is said to be "ﬁrst proposed in [31]", but [31] is Faster R-CNN.
  - The concurrent co-attention transformers are cited as "[32,33]", which are ReferIt and MAttNet.
  - RefCOCO+ is cited as [32], which is a duplicate ReferIt entry.

  Don't take an origin for co-attention from this paper.
- BERT-base's hidden size is printed as "762". It should be 768.
- The extraction of figure text is garbled, but body text and tables came out clean.
- There were no embedded instructions.
